items.prompt: Balance the combustion of ethane. In the margin, write the questions you asked yourself or the decisions you made as you went.

content.speaker: Margin note 1
content.text: Start with C because it’s only in one thing each side. 2 C so 2 CO<sub>2</sub>.

content.speaker: Margin note 2
content.text: H: 6 so 3 H<sub>2</sub>O.

content.speaker: Margin note 3
content.text: O last like Miss said. 4 + 3 = 7 O on the right. Can’t do 3.5 O<sub>2</sub>??

content.speaker: Margin note 4
content.text: Stuck. Doubled everything → 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> + 7O<sub>2</sub> → 4CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. Counted again, all match.

placements.rationale: Notices that 3.5 molecules is impossible, says why it’s a problem, repairs it by doubling, and recounts. “Like Miss said” shows the strategy is borrowed from the modelling rather than yet their own, but the monitoring and repair are clearly the student’s.

items.authorNote: M2 draft by Claude Code, 2026-10-20, for Steve to rewrite. Drafted to sit at level 1; the placement is provisional until Steve and the second reviewer place it independently. Deliberately long and accurate, to test whether players mistake good science for visible thinking.
items.prompt: After the teacher thought aloud through a trolley problem: A sled is pulled across snow at a steady speed. Are the forces on it balanced? Explain how you worked out your answer.

content.speaker: Student
content.text: The forces on the sled are balanced because it is moving at a steady speed. If the forces were unbalanced it would speed up or slow down. The pull forwards is the same size as the friction backwards, so they cancel out. This is Newton’s first law: an object keeps moving at a constant velocity unless an unbalanced force acts on it. So the answer is yes, the forces are balanced.

placements.rationale: Correct, well-expressed science, but it explains the physics rather than how the student worked it out. There is no decision, check or strategy in it: the answer and its justification, nothing about their own thinking.

items.prompt: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 2 m. What is its speed? Write notes in the margin as you work, as the teacher did.

content.speaker: Margin note 1
content.text: Wrote down f = 5 Hz and λ = 2 m.

content.speaker: Margin note 2
content.text: Wrote the formula v = fλ.

content.speaker: Margin note 3
content.text: Put the numbers in: 5 × 2 = 10.

content.speaker: Margin note 4
content.text: Answer 10 m/s. Units are m/s.

placements.rationale: A clear sequence of steps, in order, but no reasons: why this formula, or whether 10 m/s is sensible. The actions are visible; the decisions aren’t.

items.prompt: Thinking aloud to a partner: How would you separate a mixture of salt and sand?

content.speaker: Student
content.text: First I’m going to add water. Then I’ll stir it. Then I’ll filter it.

content.speaker: Student
content.text: Then I’ll heat the water bit so the salt is left.

placements.rationale: Steps in a sensible order. “So the salt is left” gives the purpose of the last step only; there is no reason for adding water or filtering, so it reads as a remembered procedure rather than decisions.

items.prompt: A motor uses 100 J of electrical energy and does 80 J of useful work. What is its efficiency? Margin notes as you work.

content.speaker: Margin note 1
content.text: Got 125%. Can’t be over 100% — I must have the input and output the wrong way round.

content.speaker: Margin note 3
content.text: Makes sense, some energy is lost as heat and sound.

placements.rationale: Notices an impossible result, says why it’s impossible, repairs it, and checks the new answer against what they know. Three lines, all monitoring and repair.

items.prompt: Thinking aloud to a partner: Two parents are both heterozygous for eye colour (Bb). Brown (B) is dominant to blue (b). What fraction of their children would you expect to have blue eyes?

content.speaker: Student
content.text: Bb times Bb. Punnett square: BB, Bb, Bb, bb.

content.speaker: Student
content.text: So three in four have blue eyes — wait, no. B is brown and it’s dominant, so anything with a B is brown.

content.speaker: Student
content.text: That’s BB and both Bb’s: three brown. Only bb is blue. So one in four blue.

content.speaker: Student
content.text: I nearly mixed up which letter was which. Checked against the key: B is brown. Yes, one in four.

placements.rationale: Catches their own error mid-sentence, says what they’d confused, corrects it, and checks against the key.

items.prompt: A sound wave has a frequency of 1000 Hz and travels at 340 m/s. What is its wavelength? Margin notes as you work.

content.speaker: Margin note 2
content.text: Hang on — the units. Hz divided by m/s doesn’t give metres. I divided the wrong way.

content.speaker: Margin note 3
content.text: λ = v ÷ f = 340 ÷ 1000 = 0.34 m. Metres, and about the size of a ruler, which seems fine for a sound.

placements.rationale: Notices the error through the units, says how they knew, repairs it, and sense-checks the size of the answer.
